items.title: Lionel Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I got Lee Young, who was Lester Young’s brother, playing drums with me.

ctx.x: Did you put him on lead then?

Yeah, he played lead. And I got Lee Young, who was Lester Young’s brother, playing drums with me. And I kept picking up men like that until I picked up a 16 piece band. And so I got some arrangements from a guy by the name of Joey Williams, who had a book of arrangements, and I got, and he was a terrific arranger. The first arrangement that, oh, what’s the big band leader’s name? What I’m going to tell you, you’re going to be shocked. Glenn Miller. This guy arranged for Glenn Miller. Because it wasn’t Glenn…
For the way the reed section worked?

items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I liked working with Hamp's band

ctx.x: How did you like working with Hamp's band?

I liked working with Hamp's band, but I got to tell you -- I ran into the same thing with myself, you know, because Hamp was a drummer, also, and he played vibes. I think I was very jealous of him, you know, being very candid about it. I'm sure that I was,,because the man really liked me, you know? He let me do anything. If we broadcasted and played 3 tunes on the air, I would sing 2 of them, you know, and he's trying to push me, you know, but as I said -- again -- sometimes it takes you a long time to grow up,…

thing. Well, you know, I had a pretty good technique, and I played from hand to hand, you know -- I didn't start everything with my right hand, you know. And so I played solos -- whichever hand was there, I would start with the left or the right hand, you know. Now an unschooled drummer starts everything with his right hand, and so we had a challenge thing called "Diggy Diggy Doo", and Hamp had a little tom tom down in front, you know, and the man worked so hard, and he had me way up here where like Sonny Greer…
